source_text: Ὡς εἰσαχθέντων πρὸ τοῦ βήματος Ῥουστικὸς ὁ ἔπαρχος εἶπε πρὸς Ἰουστῖνον· Πρῶτον πείσθητι τοῖς θεοῖς καὶ ὑπάκουσον τοῖς βασιλεῦσιν. Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ἄμεμπτον καὶ ἀκατάγνωστον τὸ πείθεσθαι τοῖς προσταχθεῖσιν ὑπὸ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ποίους λόγους μεταχειρίζῃ; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Πάντας μὲν λόγους ἐπειράθην μαθεῖν, συνεθέμην δὲ τοῖς ἀληθέσι λόγοις τοῖς τῶν Χριστιανῶν, κἂν μὴ ἀρέσκωσι τοῖς ψευδοδόξοις. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ἐκεῖνοί σε ἀρέσκουσιν οἱ λόγοι, πανάθλιε; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ναί, ἐπειδὴ μετὰ δόγματος ὀρθοῦ ἕπομαι αὐτοῖς. Ῥουστικὸς ἔπαρχος εἶπεν· Ποῖόν ἐστι δόγμα; Ἰουστῖνος εἶπεν· Ὃ εὐσεβοῦμεν εἰς τὸν τῶν Χριστιανῶν θεόν, ὃν ἡγούμεθα ἕνα τοῦτον ἐξ ἀρχῆς ποιητὴν καὶ δημιουργὸν τῆς πάσης κτίσεως, ὁρατῆς τε καὶ ἀοράτου, καὶ κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν παῖδα θεοῦ, ὃς καὶ προκεκήρυκται ὑπὸ τῶν προφητῶν μέλλων παραγίνεσθαι τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων σωτηρίας κήρυξ καὶ διδάσκαλος καλῶν μαθημάτων. Κἀγὼ ἄνθρωπος ὢν μικρὰ νομίζω λέγειν πρὸς τὴν αὐτοῦ ἄπειρον θεότητα, προφητικὴν τινά δύναμιν ὁμολογῶν· ἐπεὶ προκεκήρυκται περὶ τούτου ὃν ἔφην νῦν θεοῦ υἱὸν ὄντα· ἃ γὰρ ἄνωθεν προεῖπον οἱ προφῆται περὶ τῆς τούτου παρουσίας γενομένης ἐν ἀνθρώποις.
thought_title: Obeying Christ and stating the Christian teaching about God
orientation: Justin, the Christian teacher, is now questioned before the tribunal by Rusticus the prefect who orders obedience to the gods and the emperors.
pass_a_gloss: When they had been brought in before the tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin: First be persuaded by the gods and obey the emperors. Justin said: Blameless and not to be condemned is obeying the things commanded by our Savior Jesus Christ. The prefect Rusticus said: What teachings do you practice. Justin said: I tried to learn all teachings, but I assented to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even if they do not please those who hold false opinions. The prefect Rusticus said: Do those teachings please you, most wretched man. Justin said: Yes, since I follow them with right teaching. The prefect Rusticus said: Of what sort is the teaching. Justin said: That by which we give true worship to the God of the Christians, whom we consider this one from the beginning maker and craftsman of the whole creation both visible and invisible, and Lord Jesus Christ servant of God, who also has been proclaimed beforehand by the prophets as about to come to the race of humans as herald of salvation and teacher of good lessons. And I being a human consider it a small thing to speak in regard to his boundless deity, confessing a certain prophetic power; since it has been proclaimed beforehand concerning this one whom I just now said is Son of God; for the things which the prophets said beforehand from above concerning his coming that happened among humans.

be persuaded by and so obey here

choices.why: work brief fixes λόγος as teaching and bans philosophy and argument
work brief fixes δόγμα as teaching and bans doctrine and belief
work brief fixes εὐσέβεια as true worship and treats it as loyalty toward the true God
keeps παῖς distinct from υἱὸν son of God in the next clause and matches the cast note Son and Servant
work brief fixes σωτηρία as salvation and κήρυξ is a proclaimer of it

pass_b_english: Once they stood before his tribunal, Rusticus the prefect said to Justin, "First obey the gods and obey the emperors." Justin answered, "It is blameless and beyond condemnation to obey what our Savior Jesus Christ commanded."

The prefect asked, "What teachings do you handle?" Justin answered, "I have tried to learn every teaching, but I have given my assent to the true teachings, those of the Christians, even when they displease people of false opinions." Rusticus the prefect said, "Do those teachings please you, you utter wretch?" Justin answered, "Yes, for I follow them with right teaching." The prefect asked, "What is that teaching?"

Justin answered, "It is that we give true worship to the God of the Christians. We hold him to be the one God from the beginning, the maker and fashioner of all creation, visible and invisible. And we hold the Lord Jesus Christ to be the servant of God. He was proclaimed beforehand by the prophets as the one who would come to the human race as a herald of salvation and a teacher of good lessons. I am only human, so whatever I say is small beside his boundless divinity, and I confess I speak only with a share of prophetic power. For he whom I just called the Son of God was proclaimed beforehand, and the prophets long ago foretold his coming among humans."
notes: final clause breaks off in the source given: ἃ γὰρ ἄνωθεν προεῖπον οἱ προφῆται περὶ τῆς τούτου παρουσίας γενομένης ἐν ἀνθρώποις has no main clause; glossed only what stands without supplying an ending

last_rejected.quote: I confess I speak only with a share of prophetic power.
last_rejected.why: Justin acknowledges a certain prophetic power (that of the prophets, which he cites). The English makes him claim a share of it, and drops the hedge 'νομίζω' (I think).
last_rejected.fix: I am only human, and I think what I say is small beside his boundless divinity, though I acknowledge a certain prophetic power.
last_rejected.ruling: 'τινὰ δύναμιν ὁμολογῶν' can mean professing some power; 'share' and dropped 'νομίζω' are style, not changed doctrine
